one oddly larger cackler mixed in on the parade grounds. photos  discord discussion opened up the possibility of a Non-Richardson subspecies    EDIT with details 02/06/25:   ***Updating this from Cackling Goose to Cackling Goose (Taverner's)***  After a lot of input on the NY state discord from Aidan Kiley and Julien Amsellem on the possibility of this being a Taverner's Cackling Goose or possible intergrade Richardson's x Taverner's, I reached out to Steven Mlodinow with all my photos. His response:    "That is one of the very best Tavâ€™s that Iâ€™ve seen photographed in the eastern US. The smooth line from bill tip to crown, with very little deflection as bill/feather boundary is crossed) is key. Also, the crown is nice and rounded. The bill is hefty for a white-cheeked goose and approaching triangular, with relatively little (or no) black notch into anterior cheek strap. Note that a CACG in Alert Posture can look relatively large-headed and round-headed with a big bill, but this bird is pretty relaxed in the second photo"    This goose was initially VERY hard to pull out of the huge canada flock due it being relatively the same size as the bulk of the smaller canadas. But every once in awhile I would catch a glimpse of its very bizarre bill shape, which kept me hunting for it. I kept losing it in the crowd, but eventually singled it out and got photos of it.    It was still with the flock on the VCP parade grounds (southern end) when I left around 1pm. Input from Julian B on the bronx bird bulletin mentioned he might've seen and photographed the same bird on January 1, 2025 at VCP, so there's a chance its been staying in the area with the flock since then. Definitely worth following up on.    Thanks for all the help and input on this bird! By the looks of eBird this may be the 5th east coast record and 3rd for NY state which would be dope!

Checklist Comments: absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

Checklist Comments: wow.   1.475mil last night in bx  started off in the dark and wish I'd brought another layer.  not much in terms of morning flight (except pipit flyover)  but insane amounts of sparrow influx and myrtles everywhere. the trees were kind of dripping with them   decided to make one long checklist out of the day. north end, ballfields loop several times trying to really get an accurate census. did not go into the ballfields or around back very far. 45 min lunch/hawk watch break but no raptor activity  highlights:  crow raven trifecta!  tufted titmouse first for me at the park :)  indigo bunting target for the day came true! felt good about it too because was very bad look at first but knew it wasn't finch/sparrow like enough. later got good looks and confirmed.  huge goose flock in the early morning -- have to check photos for cacklers/white geese    record breaking species diversity day :) 53 sp including flagged pipit.  first time breaking 50 at Franz. the little park that could.  looking forward to tomorrow to see who continues

Checklist Comments: 442k migration night high  me encanto soÃ±ar  what a wild ride. skywatched from the north end from about 7-9. finally got sick of sorting through chipping and juncos so I did a quick 20 min loop of the ballfields.  when I got back to the north a birder named Art was standing there with binoculars. I said hi and he said he just had a clay colored sparrow. the bird Christine predicted would be here this morning and possibly also saw last night (if she's brave enough to submit).  he said it flushed with a big group and I proceeded to search until 12 for it to no avail. a couple of paler lored chippings, but still too dark to be clay.  then Luis from queer birders showed up on bike and we birded the last hour or so. so cool to meet him again at my home park!  while I am disappointed in no personal clay colored sparrow, I happened to ask how Art heard about this park and he said through eBird. Which by my book is a win since I've been trying all year to put this place on the birding map. if more people are checking it out, more birds are gonna get seen. so altogether a dope morning.  a bit Fetid that I didn't get to see a clay colored tho.    oh yeah and one cool partial leucistic chipper :)

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Which by my book is a win since I've been trying all year to put this place on the birding map. if more people are checking it out, more birds are gonna get seen. so altogether a dope morning.  a bit Fetid that I didn't get to see a clay colored tho.    oh yeah and one cool partial leucistic chipper :)

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Observation Details: ***alright Rare but the circumstantial evidence piled up high enough for me to feel more confident about reporting this.  was walking in the trench on 161 at 6:12am and started looking up at two gull flyovers. then saw another bird flying WNW that looked like a DCCO but something felt off. Big broad wings but flapping slowly unlike a cormie with its typical panicked wing beats. More similar to a great blue.  checked it quick with bins and saw delicate brown streaking all down an otherwise pale neck. and the "neck" of what looked like a cormorant was actually the extremely long yellow beak of a tucked in heron head. Beak seemed way too long for a night heron. And the streaking was in high contrast with the paleness of the neck.  First gut instinct was omg it's a bittern. Camera wasn't even out of my bag so I fumbled for it and autofocus really shit the bed so I have photos of white sky.  Dm'ed a few folks about it and agreed it could only be Bittern or juv night heron.  Wasn't feeling confident enough to report it, but at 8:16 it was noted on Discord that Inwood Hill park had a bittern fly into it earlier in the morning. Asked for more details and learned it flew in at approximately 6:20-25am, which by my estimation lines up perfectly with my birds trajectory and timing (about 3 miles distance in 10/15 mins). This cinched it for me, so I'm updating my report.  Huge win for Macombs Dam Park (my trash park <3) and even more inspo to get up on the roof more frequently.

Observation Details: individually counted during skywatch
Checklist Comments: 11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. Observation Details: insane.  first eBird record in the west bronx.  high up, getting mobbed by crows, and power-coasting east.  white bird with smushed in head, short fanned tail, and brown streaking on breast. photos and more details later    ***okay SO  this looks to be the 12th Bronx record of SEowl. but most notable, it's the only inland record (the others come entirely from Pelham and ferry point, in more suitable habitat)    absolutely nutso to see one in such a dense urban environment. I have not seen so many ravens together here before either, which makes me think perhaps it was following the Harlem River/Hudson down when the Ravens caught onto its tail and started mobbing it and steered it off course? Because I doubt an SEowl is willingly migrating over the grand concourse.  ***got a tip that these were in fact crows, not ravens. I assumed short eared owls were large, but it turns out they're only 14/15 inches in length, just smaller than a crow. ravens would be 24/25    anyways was about 8:00am exactly when I was coming up to the rocky hill looking at sparrows to do another north end loop. Luci saw me from far away and dashed over to say hi and I wound up chatting with Tania for awhile about some work drama.    Cut her off in the middle of a sentence when I looked up and saw an all white bird in the midst of about 6 crows. "is that a fucking owl" I said out loud and Tania asked if I meant the white one. I got camera shots of it for maybe 30 seconds while it looped around and then headed off east (hopefully to better east Bronx habitat or Suffolk).    Franz Sigel park's official second owl (counting the 1953 saw whet owl by PA Buckley). And notably we got a short eared owl on eBird before central park >:)))    bird #127 for the park and #195 for me for the BX

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Checklist Comments: bonkers day of cave swallow watching at the southern zone landfill. joined early on by rich aracil, then later by Alyssa Bueno. Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

pretty confident with this ID. Empid flying around the treetops at the southern edge of ball fields in part of the recent empid invasion wave of migrants. Good alder habitat--nothing wet/shrubby around for willows.  faint eyering--not as pronounced as the leasts that I have been seeing around the park lately. chest not dark enough for a pewee. grayish and drab overall, not enough color for acadian/yellow-bellied. Felt good for Traill's.  i used a bit of playback to see if i could get a vocalization from it, but it stayed silent. about an hour later it reappeared, flew to a far canopy, and made VERY faint pip calls. Recorded via merlin and investigated at home on Raven Lite. The call notes, while very quiet, were bell-shaped (i.e. not a straight upwards "whit" like a willow). Compared to the frequency of some macauley library pip calls and noted that they both peaked at approx. the exact same frequency range: 3700hz.  Including a short, edited section of recording here where four pips can be heard at the following time stamps: 2.14, 4.56, 6.10, 8.40. The call at 6.10 is the loudest and most diagnostic i think.  Not great at these IDs, so please let me know if this feels not quite right!    UPDATE 05/29:  Switching all photos to Least Flycatcher, but keeping the pip calls on the Alder. Did not see the bird vocalizing, so not 100% sure it was the same bird as I had photographed slightly earlier. When I went back later in the afternoon, there were at least two empids up in the same treetops. Likely a Least and an Alder confusing me.

Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Checklist Comments: bonkers day of cave swallow watching at the southern zone landfill. joined early on by rich aracil, then later by Alyssa Bueno. Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. 11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Checklist Comments: absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

Checklist Comments: 11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Checklist Comments: bonkers day of cave swallow watching at the southern zone landfill. joined early on by rich aracil, then later by Alyssa Bueno. Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

Observation Details: changing my bird sp. to pipit after the fact. During morning flight Merlin pinged a faint call as a pipit flyover. Was initially doubtful because it was a single downwards call note instead of the classic doubled "pipit" notes. But compared to some others on ebird it seems to match a single call note pretty perfectly. Downwards slash spectrogram shape going from approx 8khz down to 4khz.  Subsequent mornings have led to more pipit pings on Merlin, and Franz is on a pretty direct flight path from Randall's Island where they are frequently known to flyover, especially early AM. Still need to get eyes on one to feel really solid about it, but will take this call note for now.  #116 for the park :)

Checklist Comments: 11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

absurb record for the bronx and the park. while doing morning flight watch on the north hill photographed a bird at 7:21am flying NNW over the west edge of the park. did not strike me as unusual at the time, but going through my photos later that morning was bewildered by the stark and distinct white, yellow, and black underwing pattern in one of my photos. compared it to the underwings of RB grosbeak, scarlet tanager, goldfinch, pine siskin, and evening grosbeak. evening grosbeak matched the closest (though not exactly to the drawing), but i figured that was a ridiculous option, so i posted to discord. almost immediately was confirmed by Ryan Zucker as a female evening grosbeak.  can't believe i drove to the adirondacks last winter and dipped on these only to get them in my urban pocket park.  looks to be the 3rd ebird record for the bronx. last one in 1982 by Joe McManus at his neighborhood backyard feeders near the 5 train, and then a historical 1969 record by Georges Kleinbaum at pelham park.  ny state bird, county bird, and patch bird #118!

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

Checklist Comments: bonkers day of cave swallow watching at the southern zone landfill. joined early on by rich aracil, then later by Alyssa Bueno. Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season
