absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

Checklist Comments: bonkers day of cave swallow watching at the southern zone landfill. joined early on by rich aracil, then later by Alyssa Bueno. Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

Checklist Comments: bonkers day of cave swallow watching at the southern zone landfill. joined early on by rich aracil, then later by Alyssa Bueno. Pat also made a brief appearance.  started on the shore just south of the sparrow landfill fence. later moved south to the first beachy peninsula, then found a sweet spot in the middle of those two on the rocky shore near the big graffiti rock. this seemed to be perfectly in line with the consistent swallow flight path.  they continually appeared cresting over the eastern hills of the landfill and making a more or less direct flight across the water over towards us. theoretically it would line up in a pretty direct line with turtle cove and the lagoon at Pelham. would make sense that they are coming down the coast and then hug the lagoon side once hunter island splits off.  super exciting long bird day and memorable as heck.

Checklist Comments: absolutely stellar morning at Franz.  started at my usual spot mid park where it was a bit quiet and dark still. but heard what sounded like a great crested coming from the ball fields to the south. realized I never really check the tree line from INSIDE the ball fields, and have seen people running their dogs in there, so went to go check it out.  best decision of the day. immediately started hearing tons of warbler song, and the sun was hitting these southwest trees in full getting the bugs really active.  btgreen, mag, BTblue, yellow, and redstart were all quite readily found, a long with a vocal RBGR  biggest shocker came with a Wilson's warbler tucked deep in the lower branches. my first for the Bronx and a first of the year for me. huge win.  swallows came next with a glance at a tree swallow and good looks at a barn swallow.  hung around for an hour or so before exploring the rest of the park, which yielded some really close views of feeding Blackpolls in a reddish purple beech tree (thanks Jules)  gb heron flyover really cinched the morning.  wanted ovenbird and a thrush on the way out, so walked the Walton slopes and got my patch Swainsons :)))  most fire morning of the Franz season

11:20-1ish stationary skywatch by her majesty  then a loop of the park  chatted with madeleine.  sick day can't stop me from getting two new park birds and one Bronx bird    so rip to birdcast: it officially turned off on november 15 and we wont be graced with her presence again until March 1.  seemed like an overall big migration night though with many bluebirds, pipits, and songbirds reported all over the city.  initial plan was to celebrate being done with work by waking up at sunrise and doing morning flight at franz, then drive to pelham to meet up with rich and alyssa. but a fever intervened and i spent the night shivering, falling asleep at 4 and finally waking up at 1030 to a lot of FOMO from reports all over the city of big bird movement.    felt marginally better though, so i bundled up, got a smoothie and a sandwich and plopped down in the grass on the watch hill for a stationary 1:30 min watch.  enormously successful with one flyover pipit (picked up by merlin and then me moments later). wish i had gotten eyes on him because he sounded VERY close. would've loved a pic. N to S flight.  alyssa then posted a bluebird at pelham and i got very salty because my cold thwarted my target bird bluebird plans. it didn't help that merlin told me bluebird was my bird of the day.  but literally as i was sending her a screenshot of my BotD and complaining that i'd never see one at franz, a tuwuwuwU call came out of the sky to the W of me. i glanced down at merlin and it agreed with me: tuwuwuWU for sure.  incredibly, i got eyes and photos on a flock of 8 of them as they flew north over the NW woods of the park.  pretty quiet after that excitement. i thought bluebird was a county bird for me, but it turns out i saw one last year at pelham (where i also met hailey for the first time). but still a franz bird is just as good.    this songbird flight gave way to a slow but steady movement of raptors. many TUVU, red tailed hawks, and a bunch of extremely high up buteos I couldn't make out. I was also watching the CT group me where there were more reports of Golden Eagles drifting towards NY.    black vulture, broad winged hawk, bald eagle, golden eagle, and red-shouldered hawk were all the targets as my brain switched to raptor mode.    and lo and behold, a red-shouldered came over with a sharpie and a RTHA. beautiful orange underneath with black and white fringing to the wings and a lovely banded tail. i was worried i wouldn't recognize one if it came by, so i took a ton of pics just to be sure, but my instincts were right.    overall an amazing outcome for a late start day. welcome new franz birds 128 and 129: eastern bluebird and red-shouldered hawk <3

funny audio that sounded pretty solid for acadian, but not enough of a slam dunk to confirm. copy pasting the notes below for posterity:    Heard just north of the dog run by the old bathrooms.  Pretty explosive psew call. Running it through izotope and raven lite i came up with the following:  Peak high frequency around 6600hz, where a comparable Macauley clip peaks at around 6550hz.  Length of call note about 00.10 seconds, which matches the Macauley of 00.12 pretty well.  Going through similar "peep" call notes, Alder top frequency is 3.7khz, Yellow-bellied 5.7khz, Least would have an upwards "Whit," not a bell curve notehead. The "fitz" part of the Willow Fitz-bew can have a similar vibe, but tends to have a more shallow ascent and then a steep drop off, whereas this call note is pretty equal in ascent and descent. It would also be odd to have the Willow call just the first part of its song 4 times in a row with no "bew."  This is mostly arm chair birding from working on a birdsong app with Tom Stephenson, but I think this is a pretty convincing Acadian. Though to be fair, I'm only comparing it to flycatchers. There's probably a bunch of other similar vocalizations made by other birds im not thinking of.  Attaching unedited recording and then an amplified recording with the other frequencies deadened.

Observation Details: merlin detected a purple finch flight call. interestingly it does sound good for it. and there was a lot of finch movement this AM but i wasn't camera ready for most of the them. leaving this audio here as a reminder to keep an ear out for this noise.  cute short low chip call
Checklist Comments: 200k migration night but seems mostly like stragglers from yesterday--not much in terms of new arrivals.  morning watch on the hill, then a loop. joined by Kelsey and then did another loop.  gorgeous male towhee--only females so far so it was a nice change in plumage.  yellow rumps most abundant with a couple one off other warbler sp  not as big a group of sparrows as yesterday but still decent numbers  hooray for a new eBirder at Franz!  also met Rio in the morning which was cool. heavens yes.
